_README: TEMPLATE, not a drop-in. Merge the parts you want into your own
~/.claude/settings.json; do not copy this file over yours.
Replace <PYTHON_EXE> with an absolute path to a Python 3.10+ interpreter and
<CLAUDE_HOME> with the absolute path to your .claude directory. Claude Code
does not expand ~ or environment variables inside a hook command, which is
why these are absolute and why they are the only machine-bound values here.
The permissions block is ONE operator's threat model, published as a worked
example. Read every line before adopting it; an allowlist you did not decide
on is worse than no allowlist. The `ask` entries are the important half —
they make the config edit itself a confirmed action.
Two of the source environment's mounts are omitted rather than left
pointing at files you do not have: the external-dispatch hooks that gate a
dispatcher this share does not ship. Both are declared in
tools/share-manifest.toml with the reason. A third omission ended
2026-08-16: the SessionEnd memory-pipeline script now ships as
compact-recovery/preserve.py, but its mount stays out of this file — it
points outside hooks/, and this template mounts hooks/ and nothing else;
the optional SessionEnd block lives in compact-recovery/README.md.
Every hook in hooks/ IS mounted here — if you find one that is not, that is
a defect in this template, not a recommendation.
Verify after wiring: run each hook by hand with empty stdin and check it
exits 0 — e.g. `<PYTHON_EXE> <CLAUDE_HOME>/hooks/ops_health_nudge.py < /dev/null`.
Every hook here is fail-open, so a silent exit 0 is the healthy state.

_comment: HIGH-VOLUME matcher: one Python start (~100ms) on every Read/Grep/Glob.
Acceptable for a bounded measurement window, not as a permanent tax —
the hook's own docstring states the exit criterion. Mount it while you
want the measurement; unmount it when you have one.
compact-recovery trio, part 1 of 3 (overview: compact-recovery/README.md).
Denies an unbounded Read of large session-transcript files; the deny
message itself states the compliant grep-then-windowed-read path.
The SECOND half of ui_verify_guard.py. It is one file mounted on two
events: PreToolUse denies an unprobed screenshot, PostToolUse reads the
probe RESULT and routes on it. Mount both or the hook only denies and
never routes.
compact-recovery trio, part 2 of 3. Before the summary lands, writes a
bookmark (transcript path, line count, trigger) that the SessionStart
pointer card reads, then best-effort refreshes digest cards via
<CLAUDE_HOME>/tools/memory-pipeline/preserve.py (ships in
compact-recovery/; skip installing it and the hook silently skips the
refresh — the bookmark still works).
compact-recovery trio, part 3 of 3. Matcher 'compact' fires after both
manual and auto compaction; SessionStart stdout is injected into the
fresh context, which is what lets the pointer card reach the model.
